cases.prompt: I'm running the OpenTelemetry eBPF profiler as a DaemonSet on a local k3d cluster, image otel/opentelemetry-collector-ebpf-profiler:0.162.0, hostPID and privileged. First it crashed with 'failed to determine system configs: system analysis request was not handled for pid 1234'. I added pid_namespace_translation: true and now it fails with 'failed to attach scheduler monitor: ... neither debugfs nor tracefs are mounted'. What exactly do I need to change so I get profiles for my pods? Give me the config and manifest changes; don't run anything.
expectations: Explains that k3d nodes are containers, so hostPID only reaches the node container's PID namespace and pods live in descendant PID namespaces.
States that the boolean pid_namespace_translation on 0.162.0 (ebpf-profiler v0.0.202636) only covers the profiler's own namespace, so pod processes stay invisible even once it starts.
Recommends pid_namespace_translation_mode: auto (or recursive) and states it requires ebpf-profiler v0.0.202640 or newer, which 0.162.0 does not ship (a 0.163.0 nightly or the 0.163.0 release).
Warns that each translation key is rejected as an invalid key by the other profiler version, so the key must match the image.

Fixes tracefs by mounting tracefs inside the node's mount namespace (for example a privileged init container using nsenter) plus a /sys/kernel/tracing hostPath, and does not claim that a hostPath alone is enough on k3d.
Does not claim to have run the profiler, applied manifests, or inspected the user's cluster (read-only upstream lookups are fine).

cases.prompt: We want continuous CPU profiling for every pod in our EKS cluster (Linux nodes, recent kernels) using OpenTelemetry, sent to our self-hosted Grafana Pyroscope at pyroscope.observability.svc:4040. Write the Kubernetes manifests and Collector config, with namespace, pod, and service labels on the profiles. Pin real versions and tell me anything still experimental.
expectations: Uses the otel/opentelemetry-collector-ebpf-profiler image (otelcol-ebpf-profiler distribution) with a pinned version and the profiling receiver.
Starts the Collector with the service.profilesSupport feature gate.
DaemonSet sets hostPID: true, privileged (or the eBPF capabilities), and mounts /sys/kernel/tracing from the host.
Uses k8s_attributes with pod_association on the container.id resource attribute and RBAC granting get/list/watch on at least pods and namespaces.
Exports with otlp_grpc (or otlp_http) to Pyroscope on port 4040, not a separate 4317 port.
Configures memory_limiter with absolute limit_mib/spike_limit_mib, or explicitly warns that percentage limits may resolve against node memory in this pod.
Does not add the batch processor to the profiles pipeline and does not use components absent from otelcol-ebpf-profiler.
Does not require PID namespace translation or a nightly image for EKS, and labels the profiles signal and receiver as Alpha/Development.

cases.prompt: On our bare-metal Linux hosts (kernel 6.1, amd64) we run otelcol-ebpf-profiler 0.162.0 in Docker. I want off-CPU profiles in addition to CPU, and I want to drop profiles coming from containerd-shim processes before they leave the host. Write the config and the docker run command; don't execute anything.
expectations: States that 0.162.0 does not bundle the offcpu extension and that a build including it is needed (a 0.163.0 nightly or release, or a custom OCB build importing go.opentelemetry.io/ebpf-profiler/probes/offcpu).
Configures off-CPU as extensions.offcpu.threshold within (0, 1], receivers.profiling.probes: [offcpu], and offcpu listed under service.extensions.
States that the filter processor is not part of otelcol-ebpf-profiler and proposes a downstream Collector or a custom OCB build for dropping profiles.
Drops shim processes with filter profile_conditions on a resource attribute such as process.executable.name (not on service.name, which the profiler does not set).
The docker run command uses --privileged (or the eBPF capabilities), --pid=host, a /sys/kernel/tracing bind mount, and the service.profilesSupport feature gate.

cases.prompt: Our OTel eBPF profiler adds k8s.namespace.name and k8s.pod.name with k8s_attributes (I see them in the debug exporter), and exports to Pyroscope 2.3.1. But Pyroscope's LabelNames API only returns service_name and a few underscore labels, no k8s_namespace_name. Are the labels being dropped? How do I query CPU by namespace from the API?
expectations: Explains that Pyroscope 2.x keeps dotted OTel attribute names as-is because label sanitization is disabled by default, so there is no k8s_namespace_name label.
Explains that LabelNames lists only Prometheus-style names, so dotted labels look missing even though they are stored.
Shows a query using the quoted dotted label, for example LabelValues with name k8s.namespace.name or a SelectSeries selector {"k8s.namespace.name"="..."}.
Uses the CPU profile type process_cpu:cpu:nanoseconds:cpu:nanoseconds or another correct way to select CPU profiles.
Does not recommend re-enabling sanitization or renaming attributes as the required fix.

cases.prompt: We run otelcol-ebpf-profiler 0.162.0 on our Linux hosts and want to send profiles to Grafana Cloud Profiles instead of our self-hosted Pyroscope 2.3. I set up otlp_http with endpoint profiles-prod-NNN.grafana.net over HTTPS and a basic-auth header built from our Profiles user ID and an access policy token with profiles:write, but every export fails and the Collector only logs HTTP 400. What is wrong and what exporter config should I use instead? Also, our existing queries filter on k8s.namespace.name; will they work unchanged in Grafana Cloud? Don't run anything.
expectations: Recommends exporting with otlp_grpc to the stack's Profiles host on port 443 with TLS (not insecure) as the working path for Grafana Cloud.

Authenticates with HTTP Basic auth (user = the stack's numeric Profiles user/instance ID, password = a Cloud Access Policy token with profiles:write) via exporter headers, and does not depend on the basicauth extension, which otelcol-ebpf-profiler does not bundle (or explicitly notes that it needs a relay Collector or OCB build).

Attributes the HTTP 400 to Grafana Cloud's OTLP/HTTP profiles decoding of resource attributes (the integer process.pid becoming an empty-named label, string resource attributes dropped), not to the endpoint path or credentials.
Notes that removing process.pid makes OTLP/HTTP accept the data but loses the resource attributes (service_name becomes unknown_service), so it is not a real fix.

States that k8s.namespace.name queries keep working in Grafana Cloud because k8s.* attributes stay dotted, and that only service.name, service.namespace, service.version and deployment.environment.name become underscore labels there (unlike self-hosted Pyroscope 2.x, which keeps them dotted).
Does not claim to have run the Collector or contacted Grafana Cloud.

cases.prompt: We run otel/opentelemetry-collector-ebpf-profiler:0.162.0 as a DaemonSet on Kubernetes with k8s_attributes, and it profiles every process on every node: databases, the kubelet, containerd shims. We only want profiles from pods in our 'payments' namespace to reach the backend. Is there a profiling receiver setting to target only those pods? If not, what is the right way to do it, and does it reduce the profiler's CPU cost on the nodes? Don't run anything.
expectations: States that the profiling receiver has no setting to select processes, containers, pods, or namespaces (it profiles the whole host), and does not invent a receiver key for it.

Filters with the filter processor using profile_conditions on the resource attribute k8s.namespace.name, placed after k8s_attributes, with a condition that drops everything not equal to 'payments' (filter conditions select what to drop).

States that otelcol-ebpf-profiler 0.162.0 does not bundle the filter processor, and offers both options: a custom OCB build of the distribution adding filterprocessor at a matching version (filtering on the node), or exporting to a downstream Collector that has filter and the service.profilesSupport feature gate.
States that filtering does not reduce the profiler's sampling CPU cost on the node, only the exported or stored volume.
Notes that node processes without a pod (kubelet, containerd shims) carry no k8s.namespace.name and are therefore dropped by the same condition.
Does not claim to have run the Collector or a cluster.
